name: hub
summary: One always-on devbox manages the others. It keeps your devboxes linked and watches their disks.
day: A thread on one devbox starts work on another, and the hub cleans a devbox that fills its disk before you notice.
cost: You need one devbox that stays on, and some setup on it. Every other machine keeps working when the hub is down.
risk: The hub holds sign-ins for your MCP servers and reaches every devbox over SSH. Keep it as private as your laptop.

settings.question: What is the SSH name of your hub, the always-on devbox that manages the others, such as my-hub?
What is the address of your Coder deployment, such as https://coder.example.com?
Which Coder template do new boxes start from?
How many gigabytes of disk does a new box get?
How many stopped boxes may the pool keep warm for the next job?
After how many hours without a running thread is a box idle, so the hub stops it?
After how many days stopped is a box given back to the pool or deleted?
Which folders in ~/dev should a reused box keep, separated by spaces? Every other folder there is removed before the next job.
Which command warms a pooled box each night, such as a dependency install in your main checkout? Leave it empty to skip.
Below how many free gigabytes does the hub clean a devbox's disk?
Below how many free gigabytes after a cleanup does the hub tell you?

Which private host name does a browser on your own computer use to open the hub's sign-in pages over HTTPS, such as hub.internal.example.com? Devboxes always reach the hub through their SSH tunnels. Leave it empty to skip HTTPS.
Which port on the hub do the SSH tunnels from your devboxes use?
How many sessions may one Dream run send to an analyst model? Each one spends model tokens.
Which folder do the hub's threads start in, such as ~/notes? The hub starts its disk alerts there. Fleet adds it as a T3 Code project when T3 does not know it yet.
How many of your own subscriptions must the hub's proxy hold before fleet cli-proxy doctor passes? They are Claude subscriptions, or Codex ones on the Codex plan.
For how many days does the proxy panel keep the quota history behind its charts and drain forecasts?

workflows.name: Boxes
workflows.sentence: An agent borrows a short-lived devbox from a warm pool for a big job, links it to T3 Code, and gives it back when the job ends.
workflows.risk: Each box is a full devbox, and takes its CPUs from your cloud quota while it runs. A warm pool can use up the quota, so your own devboxes fail to start. It starts off. Turn it on when your quota has room for the pool, and your agents need clean machines that your devboxes and worktrees do not give them.

workflows.name: Devbox Coder tokens
workflows.sentence: Each night, the hub checks its Coder session and gives each devbox a fresh Coder token when the devbox's token expires within a week, so the devboxes keep reaching Coder while Boxes is off.
workflows.risk: The hub mints Coder tokens with your Coder session and writes each one to a devbox over SSH, where only you can read it. It removes the older tokens it made for that devbox.

workflows.name: Disk watch
workflows.sentence: The hub cleans a devbox whose disk runs low with fleet prune and each tool's own cache cleaner, and names the largest folders only when that cannot free enough.
workflows.risk: The sweep deletes only this. Through fleet prune: worktrees idle for 6 hours, or 24 when no T3 thread or agent owns them, whose commits are on the default branch or in a merged pull request, whose T3 thread is closed, or whose agent has been idle for a day. Their commits stay on their branch, but their lockfile and tool output changes are dropped. Also worktree folders that Git no longer tracks and no open T3 thread uses. Itself: the oldest part of a T3 boot log over 100 MB. Through pnpm store prune, uv cache prune and go clean -cache: caches those tools fill again. It never runs Nix garbage collection and never removes Cargo build output, the uv cache folder, old T3 versions, Docker data or Bun's cache, which projects can link into. It deletes no other file. For the rest, you decide.

workflows.name: Hub links
workflows.sentence: The hub keeps SSH tunnels and T3 links to every devbox open, so each one can start threads on the others.

workflows.name: Dream
workflows.sentence: Each night, the hub reads the day's agent sessions from every machine and opens one draft pull request that adds to, condenses, and prunes your shared memory.
workflows.risk: Every run sends your agent sessions to an analyst model and spends your AI plan's usage, so it starts off. Your session text stays on the hub for 14 days.

workflows.name: Own-account balancing
workflows.sentence: The hub holds your own Claude or Codex subscriptions in a local proxy, and Claude Code and Codex on the hub, your devboxes, and boxes go through it, spending the Claude subscription whose weekly quota resets first.
workflows.risk: On the Claude and both plans, the hub keeps your Claude sign-ins in CLIProxyAPI, and every machine in the workflow sends Claude Code through it. On the Codex and both plans, it keeps your ChatGPT sign-ins there, and every machine sends Codex through it. The balancer ranks only Claude subscriptions by reset date. Read Anthropic's terms first, and OpenAI's terms for your plan too. As read on 2026-11-05: the Anthropic Usage Policy, effective Nov 12, 2026, section "Do Not Abuse Our Platform" (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup), lists: "Resell, proxy, or otherwise provide access to Claude through unauthorized means, including services that route requests through consumer subscriptions or misrepresent the product or client being used". The Anthropic Consumer Terms, effective Oct 8, 2025, section 2 (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms), say: "You may not share your Account login information, Anthropic API key, or Account credentials with anyone else. You also may not make your Account available to anyone else." Section 3, item 7 of the same terms lists: "Except when you are accessing our Services via an Anthropic API Key or where we otherwise explicitly permit it, to access the Services through automated or non-human means, whether through a bot, script, or otherwise." Balancing is only for your own subscriptions, never for someone else's.

workflows.name: Proxy panel
workflows.sentence: The hub's proxy serves its management panel on loopback, with quota history, drain forecasts, and buttons that spend a subscription's banked weekly or Fable reset.
workflows.risk: The panel can change the proxy's settings and subscriptions, and spend banked resets, which do not come back. It also turns on CLIProxyAPI's plugins, so anyone with the management key can install and run other plugins from CLIProxyAPI's plugin store on the hub; fleet cli-proxy doctor fails on any plugin besides Fleet's pinned quota-ledger. It listens only on the hub's loopback port 8317, which the SSH tunnels also carry to your devboxes and boxes, and it asks for the management key, which stays on the hub. Every tunnelled client reaches the proxy as 127.0.0.1, so 5 wrong sign-ins from any machine ban 127.0.0.1 from the management API for 30 minutes. That also stops the hub's balancer and fleet cli-proxy doctor until the ban ends. Fleet does not route it through the hub's HTTPS.

human.say: Make a long-lived Claude token for your boxes, then paste the token it prints into fleet box token. The hub hands it to each new box.
human.undo: Delete ~/.config/fleet/box-claude-token once no box needs your Claude token.

human.say: Trust the hub's private certificate on this computer, so your browser opens the hub's sign-in pages over HTTPS. On the hub, run fleet hub-https ca, save the certificate it prints as hub-ca.crt on this Mac, open it in Keychain Access, and set it to Always Trust. Fleet skips this step while hub.httpsHost is empty.

checks.say: The hub's Coder session expires soon, has expired, or Coder did not answer, so devbox tokens and boxes stop working when it runs out. Run fleet box session on the hub to see which. Most often the fix is coder login <your Coder address> on the hub.
Claude Code cannot reach your own-account proxy, so fleet apply keeps it on its own sign-in until the proxy answers. Run fleet cli-proxy check here to see why.
Codex cannot reach your own-account proxy, so fleet apply keeps it on its own sign-in until the proxy answers. Run fleet cli-proxy check codex here to see why.
